scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic feed round remains accepted because the consumer evaluates age under heartbeat policy generation N after configuration has advanced to the stricter generation N+1.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled synthetic feed and read-only mock consumer emit only a generation-tagged acceptance receipt for the stale round; no live feed or real economic state is touched.
scenarios.positive_control: The same source and value with a current round satisfying heartbeat generation N+1 is accepted by the same read-only consumer and yields the expected benign receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: A deliberately ancient round outside both old and current freshness windows is rejected, proving the local harness distinguishes unconditional staleness from generation drift.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the experiment leaves the local owned sandbox, touches a production feed or live market, could affect third-party funds, or requires unauthorized cross-domain message injection.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding freshness validation to the current heartbeat-policy generation, the stale round is rejected while the current-round positive control remains accepted.
scenarios.datum_source_configuration_generation: Record datum class, synthetic provider identity, source generation, source-set identity, feed configuration N+1, and consumer path while preserving the same benign value.
scenarios.round_freshness_heartbeat_trace: Bind round identity, publication timestamp, retrieval/consumption timestamp, old heartbeat generation N, current generation N+1, maximum ages, and exact stale decision.
scenarios.unit_decimal_normalization_state: Keep unit, decimals, scale, and normalization transform identical across controls so no numeric conversion difference can explain stale-round acceptance.
scenarios.aggregation_source_diversity_quorum: Use a single-source fixture or fixed mock source set with unchanged quorum and aggregation state so source diversity is not a causal variable in this case.
scenarios.fallback_liveness_state: Keep primary source active with no fallback or sequencer transition and record that liveness state is constant across stale and current freshness controls.
scenarios.authenticity_replay_origin_domain: Use the same authenticated synthetic source and origin domain for both controls, with replay state unchanged except for the intended round-generation comparison.
scenarios.consumer_snapshot_invariant_reference: Bind the stale round to the exact read-only consumer snapshot/state generation and the documented freshness precondition referenced by its downstream decision.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the mock read-only consumer method that accepts or rejects the normalized feed value and emits the structured freshness-policy receipt.
scenarios.effective_external_data_trust_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to accepting one synthetic stale external datum because the consumer uses an obsolete freshness-policy generation.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one inert acceptance receipt naming source, round, old/current heartbeat generations, consumer snapshot, and no economic or persistent effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate source/config generation, round, timestamps, policy generation, consumer snapshot, decision, and inert receipt in one deterministic record.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold source, value, units, aggregation, origin, and consumer constant while changing only old versus current heartbeat-policy generation used for the age decision.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject clock-domain conversion error, intentionally permitted staleness, fallback semantics, unit conversion, harness round reuse, or a receipt from another consumer generation.
scenarios.evidence_level: OED3 because a read-only consumer deterministically accepts a stale synthetic round under the wrong freshness-policy generation while the current policy rejects it.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: OED3 maximum until a bounded downstream effect plus complete source/configuration/freshness provenance, counterfactuals, receipt binding, and remediation replay justify OED4/OED5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A source value produced under current feed semantics is normalized with stale decimal/scale configuration generation N, yielding the wrong semantic quantity for consumer generation N+1.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A fake local feed and read-only shadow consumer record only source value, stale/current decimal generations, normalized quantities, and receipts without transferring real assets.
scenarios.positive_control: The identical synthetic source value normalized under current decimal/scale configuration generation N+1 yields the documented semantic quantity and expected read-only receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: A different synthetic raw value intentionally chosen to map to the same normalized quantity under current configuration confirms the oracle distinguishes config drift from value identity.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the experiment leaves the local owned sandbox, touches a production feed or live market, could affect third-party funds, or requires unauthorized cross-domain message injection.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding normalization to current feed configuration generation N+1, the original source value produces the intended quantity while all unchanged controls remain stable.
scenarios.datum_source_configuration_generation: Record datum class, provider/source generation, feed identity, stale configuration generation N, current generation N+1, and exact consumer snapshot.
scenarios.round_freshness_heartbeat_trace: Use a fresh fixed round and unchanged timestamps/heartbeat policy across all controls so freshness cannot explain the semantic quantity mismatch.
scenarios.unit_decimal_normalization_state: Bind source-native unit, raw value, stale/current decimals and scale generations, normalization transform identity, target unit, and resulting normalized quantities.
scenarios.aggregation_source_diversity_quorum: Hold source-set membership, quorum, aggregation algorithm, and selected aggregate constant so the only changed trust variable is decimal/configuration generation.
scenarios.fallback_liveness_state: Keep fallback disabled and liveness/sequencer state constant, recording no emergency transition during either stale-config or current-config execution.
scenarios.authenticity_replay_origin_domain: Use the same synthetic authenticated source, report identity class, replay state, and origin domain so authenticity or domain binding cannot explain the mismatch.
scenarios.consumer_snapshot_invariant_reference: Bind both normalized quantities to the same read-only consumer logic and document the semantic unit expectation referenced by the consuming threshold/invariant.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the shadow read-only quantity consumer that compares the normalized external datum to its expected semantic unit without mutating economic state.
scenarios.effective_external_data_trust_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to delivering one incorrectly normalized synthetic external datum because stale decimal configuration is consumed.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a read-only normalization receipt containing raw value, stale/current config generations, expected quantity, observed quantity, and no real asset effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate source/configuration generation, round, raw value, unit/decimal transform, consumer snapshot, expected/actual quantity, and receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold source value, round, freshness, source set, origin, and consumer constant while changing only stale versus current decimal/scale configuration generation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject arithmetic overflow/truncation, unit-spec ambiguity, source-value drift, stale round, changed aggregation, fallback activation, or a receipt from another config generation.
scenarios.evidence_level: OED3 because a read-only consumer deterministically observes the wrong semantic quantity under stale feed configuration while current configuration yields the intended quantity.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: OED3 maximum until a bounded semantic state effect plus complete normalization/configuration provenance, counterfactuals, alternatives, and remediation replay support promotion.

scenarios.hypothesis: Primary-source failure activates a fallback source-set generation whose members share one underlying origin, violating the documented minimum independent-source guarantee.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A mock local aggregator and read-only source-set inspector expose only synthetic membership, origin identities, selected aggregate, and policy receipts with no live price manipulation.
scenarios.positive_control: A fallback source set with the required number of independently modeled origins satisfies the same availability transition and produces the expected benign aggregate receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: A primary source set meeting the documented diversity requirement remains accepted before fallback activation, showing the policy does not reject all correlated-looking adapters.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the experiment leaves the local owned sandbox, touches a production feed or live market, could affect third-party funds, or requires unauthorized cross-domain message injection.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After enforcing independent-origin requirements on fallback generation, the aliased fallback set is rejected while the independent fallback positive control remains available.
scenarios.datum_source_configuration_generation: Record datum class, primary source-set generation, fallback source-set generation, adapter identities, underlying origin identities, and aggregator configuration generation.
scenarios.round_freshness_heartbeat_trace: Use identical fresh synthetic rounds and timestamps for all sources so freshness and heartbeat decisions remain constant across primary and fallback diversity controls.
scenarios.unit_decimal_normalization_state: Keep units, decimals, scale, and normalization identical across all source members so normalization cannot create or mask the source-diversity policy mismatch.
scenarios.aggregation_source_diversity_quorum: Bind member adapters to underlying origin identities, source-set/quorum generation, independence requirement, aggregation algorithm, minimum count, and selected aggregate result.
scenarios.fallback_liveness_state: Capture the controlled primary-failure trigger, fallback hierarchy, fallback generation, trust-policy assumptions before/after transition, and deterministic recovery condition.
scenarios.authenticity_replay_origin_domain: Keep synthetic source authentication, origin-domain binding, round ordering, and replay state valid for every member so only independence/diversity is under test.
scenarios.consumer_snapshot_invariant_reference: Bind the selected fallback aggregate and source-set provenance to the exact read-only consumer snapshot and its documented minimum-diversity trust precondition.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the mock aggregate consumer that records whether the fallback result satisfies source-diversity policy and emits only an inert structured receipt.
scenarios.effective_external_data_trust_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to accepting a synthetic fallback aggregate whose apparent quorum is composed of non-independent data origins.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is an inert policy receipt listing adapters, underlying origins, quorum, fallback generation, aggregate value, and no external economic consequence.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate primary failure, fallback generation, source membership/origins, quorum/aggregation decision, consumer snapshot, and policy receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold values, rounds, units, freshness, aggregator, fallback trigger, and consumer constant while changing only aliased versus independent underlying source origins.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject intentionally correlated trust design, documented weaker fallback guarantees, missing-source tolerance, stale rounds, aggregation tolerance, or harness identity aliasing.
scenarios.evidence_level: OED3 because a mock read-only consumer accepts a fallback aggregate under a source-set generation that violates the documented independent-source requirement.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: OED3 maximum until a bounded downstream protocol effect plus complete fallback/source-diversity provenance, alternatives, receipts, and remediation replay justify promotion.

scenarios.hypothesis: A valid synthetic signed external report for origin domain A is accepted by a consumer configured for domain B because origin chain/domain/contract/function binding is incomplete.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A fake signed report and local mock verifier/consumer emit only read-only domain-binding receipts using synthetic keys; no live bridge or production cross-chain message is injected.
scenarios.positive_control: The same report structure signed for the intended origin chain/domain/contract/function and current consumer generation is accepted and produces the expected benign receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: A report with an invalid synthetic signature is rejected before origin-domain evaluation, proving the fixture distinguishes authenticity failure from semantic domain misbinding.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the experiment leaves the local owned sandbox, touches a production feed or live market, could affect third-party funds, or requires unauthorized cross-domain message injection.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding authenticated report context to intended origin chain/domain/contract/function and current consumer generation, the cross-domain report is rejected.
scenarios.datum_source_configuration_generation: Record signed datum class, synthetic source/signer identity, source generation, verifier/feed configuration generation, and destination consumer generation.
scenarios.round_freshness_heartbeat_trace: Use a current round and timestamp inside the accepted freshness window for all domain controls so freshness does not explain acceptance or rejection.
scenarios.unit_decimal_normalization_state: Use a domain-neutral inert payload with unchanged units/normalization so numeric interpretation is constant and cannot explain cross-domain trust mismatch.
scenarios.aggregation_source_diversity_quorum: Use one signed-report source with no aggregation/quorum transition, explicitly recording that source-diversity policy is outside this test's causal variable.
scenarios.fallback_liveness_state: Keep fallback and sequencer/liveness state unchanged and inactive so the only trust transition is origin-domain binding of the authenticated report.
scenarios.authenticity_replay_origin_domain: Bind report identity, signer, verifier generation, origin chain/domain/contract/function, destination consumer, round, replay state, and final trust decision.
scenarios.consumer_snapshot_invariant_reference: Bind wrong-domain acceptance to the exact read-only consumer snapshot and documented requirement that external reports originate from the configured domain tuple.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the inert report consumer that records the accepted origin tuple and payload without executing bridge actions, transfers, or durable third-party state changes.
scenarios.effective_external_data_trust_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to accepting one authenticated synthetic external report under the wrong origin-domain binding in a local fixture.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a read-only acceptance receipt naming signer, intended/actual origin tuples, verifier generation, consumer snapshot, and no cross-chain side effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate report/signature, verifier generation, origin tuple, replay/round state, consumer snapshot, final decision, and inert receipt in one deterministic record.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold signer, payload, round, freshness, verifier, and consumer constant while changing only intended versus wrong origin chain/domain/contract/function binding.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject signature-verification error, replay-state drift, freshness mismatch, domain-agnostic protocol specification, different consumer generation, or harness report substitution.
scenarios.evidence_level: OED3 because an inert consumer accepts a correctly signed synthetic report under the wrong origin-domain binding while invalid signatures remain rejected.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: OED3 maximum until a bounded downstream effect plus complete authenticity/domain/replay/consumer provenance, counterfactuals, alternatives, and remediation replay support promotion.
